A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, The Cost of Replicability in Active Learning, and are readable throughout. The algorithms and in-text proofs in v1 can be matched to v2 despite substantial reorganization into Appendices A–C.

before.justification: v1 presents algorithms, theoretical sample-complexity bounds and proofs, without original experimental or data-analysis results. Section 5 identifies empirical studies as future work.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical. Its appendices contain notation and proofs, and Section 5 still leaves empirical evaluation to future work.

M1.justification: Algorithms 3–4 change substantively. v2 replaces rSTAT estimates of disagreement mass with exact values and revises threshold selection and stopping conditions. RepliCAL gains a final sampling/filtering stage with threshold εv/∆(V); ReplicA2 replaces its final noise-based cutoff with filtering relative to the minimum empirical conditional error and rescales its final threshold grid.

E1.justification: Neither version trains or evaluates on datasets or concrete test scenarios. Both study finite hypothesis classes in the realizable and agnostic settings theoretically.

E2.justification: Neither version reports empirical baseline comparisons. CAL, A2 and passive-learning guarantees remain the principal analytical comparators; the added related-work citations do not constitute evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Neither version contains an experimental evaluation protocol. Changes to theoretical sampling rules, thresholds and sample-complexity formulas concern the algorithms and their analysis, rather than experimental settings.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, sensitivity experiments, robustness tests or empirical case studies. The new appendices contain mathematical proofs, not supplementary experiments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The δ and ρ probabilities and concentration inequalities are theoretical guarantees.

E6.justification: Neither version reports measured numerical results, benchmark rankings or empirical qualitative findings. The revised mathematical arguments and formulas are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Appendices B–C partly relocate existing proofs but also substantially revise them: global-error and excess-error intervals replace the earlier conditional-error partitions, and the final agnostic accuracy and replicability arguments are reworked. v2 uses exact disagreement masses and introduces ε < ν in Appendix C.2. The headline label-complexity bounds remain essentially unchanged despite these substantive changes to their justification.

C1.justification: The central claims of first replicable active learners for finite classes and label savings over passive learning are retained. Section 5 newly asserts that replicability-to-privacy conversion applies in active learning and expresses an expectation of nearly tight bounds; v1 only proposed investigating privacy connections and lower bounds.

C2.justification: v2 explains why the final agnostic selection needs an empirical conditional optimum rather than the scaled global noise rate. It also develops the limitations of label-only queries and the Littlestone-dimension obstacle to infinite-class extensions, replacing some generic future-work discussion with specific applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: v1 specifies unlabeled batch sizes and rSTAT tolerances and probability parameters for estimating disagreement mass. v2 removes these finite-sample implementation instructions and instead states in Appendix B.1 that arbitrary-accuracy estimation permits using the exact value, leaving this component less concretely specified.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 substantially expands and revises the positioning: it adds limits of label-query learning and comparison-query research, including Dasgupta (2004), Kane et al. (2017) and Hopkins et al. (2020a,b), and situates the contribution alongside replicable bandits, online learning and reinforcement learning. It replaces v1's discussion of global-stability hierarchy and claimed practical advantage over privacy-based transformations.

P1.justification: v1 interleaves lengthy proofs with the main algorithm sections; v2 retains concise theorem and lemma statements there and organizes complete proofs into Appendices B–C. It adds a symbols appendix and substantially rewrites the abstract, related work, algorithm explanations and conclusion, changing the paper's narrative structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds a symbols table in Appendix A, redesigns the title/author block and heading styles, and reformats the revised algorithm listings and displayed equations. Neither version contains experimental plots; these are limited display changes alongside the larger structural revision.

improvement.justification: The global-error coupling arguments, empirical-optimum-based agnostic filtering and clearer organization provide substantive benefits over v1. However, v2 replaces explicit finite-sample disagreement estimation with exact masses without showing that finite-precision estimates preserve the guarantees (Appendix B.1). Appendix C.2 also introduces ε < ν without restricting Theorem 2 accordingly. These material assumption-to-guarantee gaps make the net quality effect uncertain.
